newsitem.title: USA: US Senate rejects second chemical pact amendment.
newsitem.headline: US Senate rejects second chemical pact amendment.

text.p: The U.S. Senate, heading for approval on Thursday of an international treaty outlawing chemical weapons, rejected two of four "killer" amendments that would have prevented U.S. ratification.
The Senate rejected a provision that would have made U.S. ratification conditional on Russia's joining the pact, called the Chemical Weapons Convention. The vote was 66-34.
Earlier, the Senate voted 71-29 to strip an amendment that barred U.S. ratification until countries like Iraq, Libya and North Korea had signed up.
Later votes were to be held on moves to eliminate provisions that would call for renegotiating a part of the treaty and for standards of verification against cheating that could not be met.
The treaty's eventual approval by a two-thirds majority vote late on Thursday was seen as assured when Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott said he would vote for it.
